target_customer: Individuals and employers who want a low fee donor-advised fund, plus workplace giving programs
problem: Traditional donor-advised funds were built for wealthy donors with high minimums and fees; Charityvest made a DAF accessible to anyone with simple pricing.
business_model: Subscription and asset-based fees on a donor-advised fund, plus corporate workplace giving

founders.name: Stephen Kump
founders.background_notes: Over ten years as a strategy consultant to nonprofits and philanthropists; idea formed at Yale in 2016 per launch coverage

exit.acquirer: Foundation Source (acquired Vennfi, the technology parent of Charityvest)

technical_complexity.rationale: A DAF needs custody, investment and grant-making rails and tax receipting, which is mostly integration and compliance work for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Operating as a 501(c)(3) DAF sponsor with its own compliance and grant rails is slower to copy than a typical app, but giant sponsors could cut fees.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not copy it directly; Daffy launched a similar low fee DAF in 2021, and the company was absorbed into Foundation Source in 2024.

market_need_then: DAFs were a fast-growing giving vehicle but gated by fees and minimums; no dated source quantifying demand at the 2019 to 2020 founding was found beyond the company's own pitch.

branding.domain_note: Used charityvest.org; the technology company operated as Vennfi.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as modern, purposeful giving (site title: Modern donor-advised funds for purposeful giving)

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive compound name, but no sourced press about the brand itself, and the parent used a separate name (Vennfi).

outcome_analysis: Charityvest, run through its parent Vennfi, raised about 5.6 million dollars across a pre-seed, a 2020 seed and a 2022 extension while serving donors and workplace giving programs. In October 2024 Foundation Source bought Vennfi to power DAF products, with Charityvest staying a separate nonprofit; founder Stephen Kump joined Foundation Source. A single data profile claims a 2025 GTCR deal, which is unverified. The outcome looks like a modest strategic sale of the technology rather than a venture-scale exit.
notes: The acquired entity was Vennfi, the parent; Charityvest itself continues as an independent nonprofit. Total raised varies by aggregator (5.73M or 6.9M); a newswire headline says 3.7M, probably cumulative. Signalbase claim of GTCR acquisition in 2025-07 is unverified and excluded. Competitor list left empty: Fidelity, Schwab and Vanguard Charitable were incumbents but the only sources found were dated 2022, and Daffy launched in 2021, after founding. Pre-seed date is 2020 per press release, month not confirmed.
